text: Git branching is an important part of version control workflow. A branch lets you work on new features without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build and test new ideas safely. When the work is finished, the branch is merged back into the main branch. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This process helps catch mistakes early and keeps the project organized. Branches also make it easier for several people to work at the same time. Learning how to use branches well is a key skill for anyone working with Git.
